utterances.text: Go now, please, to the second part of this entry. You're telling us, aren't you, that people were leaving voluntarily on account of NATO, and we then have this passage that the accused relied on to show some human sympathy, I suspect, where you wrote this - you wrote this: "There's nothing sadder than to watch a convoy of poor people who are leaving their houses according to someone's order." Whose order?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The police's order? Whose order?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the police's order. Orders of the terrorists --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- only. There were examples when Siptars themselves stated that the terrorists had forced them out of their homes, and they even punished those who didn't want to leave their villages. I can tell you about the entire village of Jakoc [phoen] that was threatened and told to leave. So I had to send part of my platoon to protect the civilian population who managed to persuade the villagers not to move out. After that, we reinforced patrols in that area, although it was not my unit's area of activity. And the villagers stayed on in that village until the very end. I also told you that at my command post in Zub village there were a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... very first entry of your daily reports, one of the only ones we've been able to, as it were, find any relevance for because there were so few entries, but the one that says in the zone of your part of the 549th Brigade the activities and movements of the terrorists were not noticed. And you do remember, don't you, that you have time and time again said that there were no terrorists in Bela Crkva. The order to move people came from the police and/or from you, and what you're writing here is a giveaway reflection of what even to you is a sad truth. Hmm?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not true at all. It's your interpretation of my words --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... still in your hand.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- distorted as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In your hand, the 31st of March, and the Court can see the wording in which we're interested on the fourth line, so I'll get the witness to read out the first two sentences. Will you please read out the first two sentences of this entry.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the orders of the brigade command, at 10.30 part of the unit was sent to carry an intervention on the axis of Orahovac-Ostrozub village. By 1800 hours search and cleaning of Ostrozub village and Madjare village were carried out. Especially strong resistance was offered by Siptars from Madjare village, but the commander of the 2nd SV, Staff Sergeant Srdjan Stojiljkovic, used a skilful manoeuvre and strike in the flank to come into a favourable position -- to arrive at a favourable position. A group of seven terrorists was blocked in one house and destroyed by tank fire. The unit spent the night outside Janciste village."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed a bit because the witness was reading a bit too fast. And the last sentence was: "An inventory of materiel and vehicles was made." The missing part was --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Here we have a reference to conflict. I think it's probably the first reference to conflict that we've found. Seven terrorists were blocked, and I think destroyed by tank fire. But this was in the course of a cleansing operation or cleaning operation of Ostrozub and Madjare, yes?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was part of a broader operation that continued immediately upon completion of that anti-terrorist action in the area of Orahovac, Velika Krusa, Bela Crkva. It was in the framework of that anti-terrorist operation that part of my unit was engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This entry ends again, does it not, with a record of a satisfactory result, and then it says this -- I must suggest to you it's a record of a satisfactory result: "In the course of the day, around a thousand people went in the direction of the border crossings. Around 70 tractors were left in the village Zub. Vehicles and technical goods were listed." So you got rid of another thousand people.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true that I was getting rid of them. They were leaving on their own accord. Tractors and technical goods remained only when people insisted on crossing at Cafa Prusit and didn't want to Vrbnica border crossing, for reasons known only to them because Vrbnica would have allowed them to cross in vehicles. And if I had any say in it, I would have prohibited them from crossing there mainly for the reason that it created an additional problem for me, because I had to issue an order to create a passage through the minefields so that these people could pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Finally, in your own hand, 1st of April -- or finally on this point in your own hand and nearly finally for the diary. 1st of April: "Unit continued its assignment until 1500 hours, completed search and cleaning or cleansing of the village Janciste, and co-acted with MUP forces in cleaning village Pagarusa and Milanovic." It's more ethnic cleansing, isn't it, and it's as simple as can be, and it's in your own hand.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not ethnic cleansing at all, Mr. Nice. At the beginning, in my set it's number 2, an order from the corps commander related to the deployment of forces, and during the -- your examination you mentioned yourself Malisevo and Dragobilje as the greatest terrorist strongholds, and you were right about that. All we did was to continue the anti-terrorist action on that axis. There was no ethnic cleansing nor did anyone receive such an assignment, nor will you be able to find that in a single document of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This day's entry is very successful, isn't it, because in the course of the day 2.000 people went in the direction of the border crossing. That's how the entry ends.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An entry cannot be either successful or unsuccessful. My entry reflects the actual state of affairs. I only noted that on that day a certain number of people crossed. And let me remind you that these figures are approximate, because nobody did a head count or checked exactly how many of them passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 2nd of April -- please look at the 2nd of April and please confirm that there is no entry on the 2nd of April of any bombing of Nogavac by NATO.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there could be no such entry because I can't talk about Nogavac, which is not in my defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- area. I didn't mention Belgrade or Pristina either. No sense in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Fourth entry: On this day 4.000 civilians went in the direction of the border crossing Cafa Prusit, transport was organised for the elderly -- for the children and the elderly, no reference to the children's parents, and then a reference to overflights in the night. So again, this was an organisation by you of transport for some elderly people and some children, was it?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the way you interpret it, although I have explained to you in detail what that implies. I explained to you also that one vehicle only was engaged to bring elderly people up to the border crossing. And even --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- my soldiers helped them pass along that path which was a passage through the minefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... on the board if you possibly -- oh. All right. This is a map that we've just made available. Would you take the pointer, please. If the -- it's a little distance for the Court, and if the audiovisual could focus on the centre of the map, where there are coloured marks, please. There are only two colours of significance. I don't know if we can get any closer than that. Thank you very much. Coming on nicely. Blue. Will you confirm that the blue marks, which we can see on this map and I'll try and get it better copied for tomorrow, are the places Drenovac, Madjare, Dragobilje, Malisevo and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we can't hear you any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll say it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you confirm, please, that the blue marks at the top are the villages of Drenovac, Madjare, Dragobilje, Malisevo and Nisa?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to stand up. Just a second. We can see Malisevo, Dragobilje, Madjare, Drenovac, and Nisa village, if I'm reading correctly, because this is a photocopy of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Djakovica --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm surprised you don't have the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- we can see -- yes.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djakovica is right here, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When you started your march, you started your march from just south-west of Djakovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period are you referring to? You must be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the 25th of March. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I set off in a completely opposite direction --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from Zub village --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You came through Djakovica and then you came to this area. Thank you very much, just point it out. That's fine. Now, meanwhile were you aware, and we can look at this in more detail tomorrow, that General Delic had set up border protection lines to the south-east and north-west of the area that you were going into? That he'd set up blockades along Retimlje and Dobrodeljane and Pagarusa? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not exactly the way you read it. You'd better read from the assignment. What was blocked was a broader area south-east and north-west of Orahovac. That's the area I'm showing now. And it's precisely indicated in the order of the brigade commander and the corps commander as well. I can find it, read it, and show you the blockade line --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... minute.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- precisely. It was --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I want your help so we can understand in simple terms what was going on, if we can look at the map again, and I'll get the map better copied for tomorrow for use on the overhead projector. The road that we can see in the bottom left-hand segment of this map, running north-west/south-east, is the only route that takes people out of Kosovo into Albania. It goes directly south-east through Prizren and then it turns south-west and it goes to the Cafa Prusit border crossing that we've heard; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. This first road, if that's what you mean, goes from Prizren to Vrbnica border crossing. And the road that I was referring to, where my unit was, goes from Djakovica through Brekovac village via Zub village to the border crossing of Cafa Prusit. And they are in no way related, these two roads. And incidentally, in every normal state, civilians, citizens, can cross the border only at border crossings. I don't see what's odd about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... this morning or this afternoon. You see, what happened, and I'll get it drawn better for you for tomorrow, is that Delic had the area guarded so that people couldn't escape save down one road. None of you went to attack the blue villages, which were the KLA strongholds. All you did was focus on and cleanse the villages that lay within the area from which they could not escape. The KLA to the north, Delic to the north-west or the south-east, and they were driven out on that road, and that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we have to stop at 1.43.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I understand. I have guessed as much and I have focused my last question on that with that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to ask you that because I couldn't remember the -- this entire question until tomorrow. What you just said is not correct. I only wrote in my war diary the direction of movement and action of part of my unit. And the number engaged was 50 to 70 men, I can't remember precisely, and one firing platoon of mortars, 120-millimetres. And if you look at the statements concerning this anti-terrorist operation, you will see that the objective was to lift the blockade off this very important road that goes through Orahovac, Milanovic towards Pristina. So there was no expulsion of population at all. There was no mention of that. The only objective was to prevent and fight terrorist action, because this road is very important. It is the shortest route from Pristina to the Beli Drim river valley, and it opens possibilities of action towards Prizren, Djakovica, and Pec. That's the only thing our unit was doing there. It was not driving the population away, as you seem to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... tomorrow, and I shall probably restrict myself to dealing with one, or at the most I have two other locations tomorrow, and I shall be finished with this witness as soon as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Nice. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of November, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
